# A Steady Map and the Right Quake

This release fixes three things that 1.6.0 still got wrong: the map no longer jumps and ignores taps whenever anything in Home Assistant changes, the notification blueprint announces the quake that is actually new, and a quiet place now also tells you when its "no quakes" result is outdated.

## Card

- **The map stays put and answers taps while Home Assistant updates.** Before, until you had panned the map yourself, every state change anywhere in your instance re-fitted it and blocked it for a moment, so on a busy instance a tap on a marker often did nothing. Now the map only re-fits when the earthquakes themselves change. _[#58]_
- **The card also warns about outdated data when nothing matches.** Before, the warning icon only appeared next to a list of quakes. A quiet place whose updates kept failing went on saying "No earthquakes match the filter" with no hint that this was old news. Now the same icon and tooltip appear next to that text while the data is stale. _[#58]_

## Sensor

- **An empty result is flagged as stale, too.** Before, the sensor only set `stale: true` while it held earthquakes, so a failed poll after a "no quakes" result looked like fresh data. Now `stale: true` is reported in both cases until the next successful poll. _[#58]_

## Blueprint

- **Only a tsunami flag makes a "Tsunami Alert".** Before, a `yellow`, `orange` or `red` impact level also got that title, so an inland quake with an orange impact level was pushed as "Tsunami Alert". Now such a notification is titled "Earthquake Alert". The "tsunami or impact alerts only" option still counts both, as before. _[#58]_
- **The notification is about the quake that is new.** Before, the blueprint only looked at the newest quake in the list. When that quake was withdrawn, the previous one moved to the top and was announced a second time, and a poll that brought a weak new quake together with a stronger, slightly older one checked only the weak one against your minimum, so nothing was sent. Now the blueprint picks the strongest quake that was not in the list before, and place, magnitude, distance and the alert flags come from that quake. _[#58]_

## Upgrading

- Update the integration and the card as usual. Restart Home Assistant after the integration update, and reload the page so the new card loads.
- **Re-import the blueprint to get the blueprint fixes.** Home Assistant copies a blueprint when you import it, so updating the integration does not change it. Use the import button in the README, or import `earthquake_notify.yaml` again and confirm the overwrite. Your existing automations keep their settings.
